newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Tuesday:

* Betty Shabazz, the wife of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, and a leader in her own right, died three weeks after receiving extensive burns in a fire that authorities said was set by her grandson.
* New guidelines are being set to define diabetes that lowers the acceptable levels of blood sugar.
* The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that public school systems are allowed to send teachers into parochial schools to teach remedial and supplemental classes to needy children.
* The U.S. Supreme Court refused to review a subpoena that orders White House lawyers to hand over notes they took in conversations with first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton in the Whitewater case.
* Louisiana's Legislature has enacted a law that allows a new and more binding form of marriage contract that severely restricts when a divorce would be permitted.
* Cigarette makers may have been hampered in their marketing efforts in the U.S. from the recent tobacco settlement, but they may have other frontiers: Eastern Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

* James Velez, who has lived in institutions since he was 7 years old because he has an uncontrollable urge to scratch himself, moves into his first apartment at age 22 in hopes of re-entering society.
